_comment: The rods an arc will throw from -- **bare copper ones, and that is the whole of the rule**.
26.2 gave the lightning rod the rest of copper's weathering, so there are eight of them where there
was one, and `minecraft:lightning_rods` gathers all eight. Filtering a mast with vanilla's tag would
say a green rod throws, which contradicts `carries_electric_current`: oxide is an insulator there, and
which stage conducts is the mechanic rather than an implementation detail (Jonah, 2026-09-20).
Waxed is in, for that file's reason -- wax keeps copper bare rather than covering it.
**It is not redundant, though nothing oxidised can reach it today.** A mast is filtered out of a mass
that `Arcs.copperAround` already walked by `carries_electric_current`, so a green rod is excluded twice
over. That is exactly why this exists: the outer rule is the one a pack can change, and a rod that
started conducting should not silently start throwing as well.
